learningObjectives.title: The Hundred Years' War and taxation
The Black Death and its effects

questions.q: The Hundred Years' War between England and France began in:
questions.explain: The war began in 1337 under Edward III over claims to the French throne and lands.

questions.q: The English king at the start of the war was:
questions.explain: Edward III pursued claims in France, launching the Hundred Years' War.

questions.q: A famous English victory in 1346 was the Battle of:
questions.explain: At Crecy (1346) English longbowmen defeated a larger French army.

questions.q: The Black Death reached England in:
questions.explain: The plague arrived in 1348-9, killing a large share of the population.

questions.q: A major economic effect of the Black Death was:
questions.explain: With so many dead, surviving workers were scarce and could demand more.

questions.q: After the Black Death, surviving peasants were able to:
options: Demand higher wages and better conditions
questions.explain: Labour shortages increased peasants' bargaining power.

questions.q: The Statute of Labourers (1351) tried to:
questions.explain: Landowners used the law to stop peasants demanding higher pay.

questions.q: A key cause of the Peasants' Revolt of 1381 was:
questions.explain: Repeated poll taxes, falling on rich and poor alike, sparked outrage.

questions.q: The radical priest who preached that all people were equal was:
questions.explain: John Ball's sermons on equality inspired the rebels.

questions.q: The leader of the Peasants' Revolt was:
questions.explain: Wat Tyler led the rebels' march on London in 1381.

questions.q: Wat Tyler was killed during a meeting with the king at:
questions.explain: Tyler was killed at Smithfield during negotiations with Richard II.

questions.q: The young king who faced the Peasants' Revolt was:
questions.explain: The teenage Richard II confronted the rebels in 1381.

questions.q: Peasants particularly resented the poll tax because it:
options: Was a flat tax that hit the poor hardest and was repeated
questions.explain: The same charge per person burdened the poor disproportionately.

questions.q: The Hundred Years' War contributed to unrest at home because it:
options: Required heavy taxation to fund the fighting
questions.explain: War costs led to unpopular taxes such as the poll tax.

questions.q: Although the Peasants' Revolt was crushed, it was significant because it:
options: Showed growing discontent, and the hated poll tax was abandoned
questions.explain: The revolt failed immediately but the poll tax was dropped and it signalled change.

questions.q: The Statute of Labourers angered peasants because it:
options: Tried to stop them benefiting from the labour shortage
questions.explain: Peasants resented laws blocking the higher wages the plague had made possible.
